themes.title: General – Power / Grid Equipment & Energy Transition

hero.oneLiner: RIR delivered 36% YoY revenue growth and 77% EBITDA growth in Q2FY26, driven by strong demand in railways, defense, and renewables, while making concrete progress on its 618-crore SiC ecosystem — with Phase 1 EPI reactor commissioning slated for January 2026 and NSE listing by March 2026, positioning it as India’s first domestic SiC wafer producer.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: SiC EPI wafer production: 150mm line, 4000 wafers/month capacity; Target thickness: 30-180 microns (3.3kV-20kV range); Current output: 10,000 devices shipped to Indian Navy (Q2FY26) via Taiwan contract manufacturer; Revenue mix: 65% export, 35% domestic; Input cost: $250/substrate; Selling price: $800 (50um) to $1500 (180um); Yield: 85% target

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not disclosed; LOIs secured from Alpha Omega Semiconductor, ST Microelectronics, Microchip for SiC EPI wafers

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: Targeting ₹8-10cr from EPI in FY26, ₹60cr+ in FY27; Margin: Expecting gradual improvement to 18-20% by FY27; Order inflow: LOIs from Alpha Omega, ST Micro, Microchip; Capex/commissioning: ₹106cr for EPI phase (Jan 2026 commissioning), ₹100cr for packaging, full 618cr ecosystem by FY28

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into 3.3kV+ IGBTs for Indian Railways and HVDC grids; Potential licensing of IP to domestic OEMs; Export market penetration via LOIs with global players; Future 200mm readiness (long-term, post-FY28)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin expansion driven by higher-value SiC EPI mix (vs legacy silicon devices), improved operational discipline, and lower outsourced manufacturing costs; Cost pressure from global transformer lead times (33kV to 1MW step-down) delaying power supply to Bhubaneswar fab; EPI gross margin expected to exceed 60% at scale

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority: Fund Phase 1 EPI/packaging (₹225cr) via equity (₹85cr done) + debt (₹30cr target); Next: Secure ₹200cr Odisha grant for Phase 2 (device fab); Explore strategic investor infusion for long-term capex; NSE listing to unlock valuation and reduce equity dilution

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, technically detailed, and execution-focused; Management emphasizes India’s first-mover advantage in medium/high-voltage SiC; Acknowledges execution risks but highlights strong academic partnerships (TIFR, IITs) and government support; Tone on NSE listing and MD appointment is urgent but non-committal on exact dates

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Power supply delay to Bhubaneswar fab (33kV to 1MW transformer lead time); Delay in MD appointment (targeted by Dec 2025); Execution risk in achieving 85% EPI yield; Geopolitical disruption in Taiwan contract manufacturing; Debt funding delays; Competition from subsidized Chinese SiC players

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: RIR is already shipping qualified SiC devices to Indian Navy using Taiwan-manufactured wafers — proving commercial viability before domestic fab is live; The company’s focus on 3.3kV+ (not EV-focused 1200V) avoids direct competition with Chinese giants; Academic partnerships (TIFR, IITs) are being leveraged for process know-how, not just funding
